items.title: Complete silence after submission
items.content:
# Complete silence after submission

No automated receipt, acknowledgement, rejection, or recruiter outreach is received following application submission.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the application was reviewed by a human.
- Does not prove the role was cancelled or already filled.
items.summary: No automated receipt, acknowledgement, rejection, or recruiter outreach is received following application submission.

probes.action: Check email spam and security quarantine folders for ATS automated acknowledgement tokens.
probes.expected_signal: Confirms whether application was ingested and generated a confirmation ID.

specimens.label: ATS status history
specimens.context: exported by the candidate on day 41

lines.text: Application received — Senior Backend Engineer
Status: Under review
Status: Under review

specimens.reading: The record shows one state change and then nothing. Silence here is the absence of an event, not an event with a hidden meaning.

specimens.label: Follow-up message to the listed contact

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Hello — I applied for the Senior Backend Engineer role on the 3rd and wanted to check the application went through. Happy to send anything else that helps.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Following up on the note above. If the search has been paused or filled, that is completely fine — I would just like to close the loop on my side.
— no reply —

specimens.reading: Two polite, dated attempts and no response. What is established is the absence of a reply, not a decision about the candidate.

perspectives.sees: One status line on day 0, the same status line on day 41, and no reply to two dated follow-ups sent to the listed contact.
perspectives.reads: The record establishes that no reply arrived. It does not carry a reading of the application, because no event after submission is in it.
perspectives.does: Records the confirmation ID and both follow-up dates, checks spam and quarantine for the receipt, and keeps other processes running to their own timelines.

perspectives.sees: The application sits in a queue whose depth exceeds the week's screening capacity. A follow-up sent to a listed address may not be attached to any requisition.
perspectives.reads: An unread application is a position in a queue, not a decision that has been taken and withheld.
perspectives.does: Works the requisitions closest to their fill date first, because time-to-fill is measured and time-to-clarity is not.

perspectives.sees: A record whose status has not changed since ingestion, and an expiry timer running against the threshold the customer's configuration sets.
perspectives.reads: An unreviewed record approaching its expiry threshold. Whether the profile was read, or was readable at all, is not a field the platform holds.
perspectives.does: Expires the record at the threshold and sends whatever the customer's notification settings specify, which may be nothing.

non_inferences: Does not prove the application was reviewed by a human.
Does not prove the role was cancelled or already filled.

items.title: Generic "closer alignment" rejection template
items.content:
# Generic "closer alignment" rejection template

Standard automated email stating the team decided to proceed with candidates whose profiles more closely match role requirements.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish which specific skill was deemed insufficient.
- Does not establish whether a human reviewer read the full resume.
items.summary: Standard automated email stating the team decided to proceed with candidates whose profiles more closely match role requirements.

probes.action: Compare CV keyword density with exact requirement phrases in the published job description.
probes.expected_signal: Reveals potential vocabulary mismatch between candidate phrasing and ATS rubric.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Update on your application

lines.text: Thank you for your interest in our company and for the time you invested in the process.
After careful consideration we have decided to move forward with candidates whose profiles more closely align with the requirements of the role.
We wish you the best in your search and encourage you to apply for future openings.

specimens.reading: Nothing in the text is specific to this candidate, this conversation or this role. The message is a routing decision rendered as prose.

specimens.label: Request for specifics, and the reply

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Thanks for letting me know. If it is possible, I would value one line on which requirement was the gap — it would genuinely help me aim better.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Unfortunately we are not able to share individual feedback. It was a very competitive process.

specimens.reading: The follow-up returns the same shape of answer. A template that survives a direct question is a policy, not an opinion about you.

perspectives.sees: A message sent at 03:14 with no sentence specific to this candidate, this role or this conversation, and a follow-up that returns the same wording.
perspectives.reads: The text is the standard wording for this outcome. Which requirement was the gap is not stated in it, and asking returned the template again.
perspectives.does: Records the date and the exact wording, and compares the CV phrasing against the requirement phrases as published, since the message names no gap to work from.

perspectives.sees: A rejection step in the queue and, afterwards, a request for one line of specifics.
perspectives.reads: The wording is the one approved for this outcome; what the panel scored beyond a recommendation is not in the recruiter's record either.
perspectives.does: Sends the approved wording and answers within it, because anything more specific is quoted back afterwards as a stated reason.

perspectives.sees: One approved wording covering every rejection at every stage, and the disclosure rule that fixes what may be given as a reason.
perspectives.reads: Identical wording across all outcomes is what makes each of them consistent and defensible if any one is challenged.
perspectives.does: Sets the template once for the whole funnel; the hours a candidate spends inferring a reason from it are not a figure this layer holds.

non_inferences: Does not establish which specific skill was deemed insufficient.
Does not establish whether a human reviewer read the full resume.

items.title: Position closed after final interview without hire
items.content:
# Position closed after final interview without hire

Candidate completes all interview rounds, but is informed that the requisition has been cancelled, frozen, or closed.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove candidate failed technical or behavioral evaluations.
- Does not prove the company lied about opening intention.
items.summary: Candidate completes all interview rounds, but is informed that the requisition has been cancelled, frozen, or closed.

probes.action: Politely inquire with recruiter if the position was closed due to business budget restructuring or team reallocation.
probes.expected_signal: Clarifies whether barrier was candidate-specific or macroeconomic/budgetary.

specimens.label: Final round, closing minutes
specimens.context: minute 47 of 50, four days before the email below

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: That is everything from our side. Any questions for us?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Only about timing — what happens next?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: We are wrapping up the loop this week. You are the last of three finalists, so expect to hear back by Friday at the latest.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. Thank you for the time.

specimens.reading: The process was described as live and near a decision. Whatever happened next happened after this point, not before it.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Regarding the Senior Backend Engineer search

lines.text: Thank you again for the conversations over the past six weeks — the panel was consistently positive about your work.
I am writing with disappointing news: the requisition has been put on hold as part of a wider planning review, and we will not be filling the role this quarter.
This is not a reflection on your interviews. If the role reopens I would like to come back to you first.

specimens.reading: The stated cause sits above the hiring loop entirely. A candidate cannot pass or fail a budget review.

perspectives.sees: A final round described in its closing minutes as one week from a decision, and an email four days later naming a planning review as the cause.
perspectives.reads: The stated cause sits above the interview loop. What the panel concluded did not determine the outcome, and the six weeks are already spent.
perspectives.does: Records the dates, the panel's own stated position and the wording of the close, and asks whether the requisition was frozen or cancelled.

perspectives.sees: A loop they ran to its end, a panel recommendation they can act on, and a requisition removed from the plan by a decision taken elsewhere.
perspectives.reads: The outcome of the loop no longer decides anything. The gap the role exists to absorb is still open and still covered by the team.
perspectives.does: Keeps the shortlist and returns to the same names if the requisition comes back, because funding it is not something this role controls.

perspectives.sees: Open requisitions as funded line items in a planning review held on a quarterly cycle.
perspectives.reads: An approved requisition that can be paused costs less than one that cannot; pausing is the instrument the approval was written to allow.
perspectives.does: Puts the requisition on hold. The stage each candidate had reached is not a field the review carries.

non_inferences: Does not prove candidate failed technical or behavioral evaluations.
Does not prove the company lied about opening intention.

items.title: Materially similar role reposted shortly after rejection
items.content:
# Materially similar role reposted shortly after rejection

Candidate observes the same or near-identical job listing reposted or refreshed on job boards within 1–8 weeks of rejection.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the role was a "fake" or "ghost" posting.
- Does not establish that the prior interview feedback was fraudulent.
items.summary: Candidate observes the same or near-identical job listing reposted or refreshed on job boards within 1–8 weeks of rejection.

probes.action: Check job listing requisition ID or ask recruiter whether the posting is an automated ATS refresh or a distinct headcount opening.
probes.expected_signal: Distinguishes between automated job board bot refreshes and genuine recurring hiring demand.

specimens.label: The two postings, side by side
specimens.context: rejection on 14 March, repost seen on 2 April

lines.text: 14 Mar — Senior Backend Engineer · Payments · Remote (EU) · 5+ years · Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka · req #4471
2 Apr — Senior Backend Engineer · Payments · Remote (EU) · 5+ years · Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka · req #4471
Body text identical except for the posted date. Same requisition number, same team, same band.

specimens.reading: The requisition number is the thing to record. A refreshed listing and a genuinely new headcount look identical on the board and are different facts underneath.

specimens.label: Asking the recruiter directly

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I saw req #4471 posted again this week. Is this a second opening on the team, or the same one refreshed?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Good catch — the board auto-refreshes listings after 30 days so they stay visible. Same requisition, still open.

specimens.reading: One question separated an automated refresh from a real second opening. This is the cheapest probe in the whole registry.

perspectives.sees: The same requisition number, team and band on a listing whose posted date has moved, with the body text otherwise unchanged.
perspectives.reads: A refreshed listing and a second opening look the same on the board. The requisition number is what separates them, and one question resolved which it was.
perspectives.does: Records both dates and the requisition number, and asks the recruiter directly, which costs one message.

perspectives.sees: One requisition record and a syndication schedule that re-posts a listing when it passes the configured interval.
perspectives.reads: Whether a listing stays in the visible window on a board is a distribution setting. Nothing about who was rejected enters that path.
perspectives.does: Refreshes the posted date on the interval the customer's configuration sets, and the board shows the listing as new.

perspectives.sees: The same requisition open on their own board with an unchanged number, and a question about it in the inbox.
perspectives.reads: The repost is the board's refresh cycle rather than a decision anyone took after the rejection.
perspectives.does: Answers it, since the requisition number and the refresh interval are facts that cannot be quoted back as a commitment.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the role was a "fake" or "ghost" posting.
Does not establish that the prior interview feedback was fraudulent.

items.title: Compensation band reduced or altered mid-process
items.content:
# Compensation band reduced or altered mid-process

Offered or discussed compensation band is revised downward from previously agreed or advertised range.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove intentional bait-and-switch malice unless verified by company policy evidence.
items.summary: Offered or discussed compensation band is revised downward from previously agreed or advertised range.

probes.action: Request clarification on whether the revised band reflects a lower leveling grade or a company-wide budget adjustment.
probes.expected_signal: Separates leveling evaluation outcome from company financial constraints.

specimens.label: Recruiter message before the offer call

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Quick heads-up before we talk numbers tomorrow — where did we land on expectations?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Same as the range in the posting and what we agreed at the screen: 85–95k.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Right. So finance has revised the band for this level since we opened the role. We are working with 72–78k now.

specimens.reading: The number moved after the candidate had already spent the process. Note the date the original band was stated and by whom.

specimens.label: Offer call, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Was the change specific to me, or to the level?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: To the level. Everyone coming in at this grade this quarter is on the new band.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: And the posting still shows the old range?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: It does. I will get that updated.

specimens.reading: An answer that generalises to the whole grade describes a policy. An answer that is specific to you would describe an assessment. They are different mechanisms.

perspectives.sees: A band stated in the posting and again at the screen, a lower band stated in week five, and the posting still showing the first figure.
perspectives.reads: An answer that applies to everyone at the grade describes a policy; an answer specific to this candidate would describe an assessment. The reply given was the first.
perspectives.does: Records the original band, the date it was stated and who stated it, and asks whether the revision is to the level or to this offer.

perspectives.sees: A revised grid for the level, arriving after the role opened, and a candidate holding the figure stated at the screen.
perspectives.reads: The number changed above the recruiter's position; the earlier figure is the one the candidate is holding going into the offer call.
perspectives.does: States the current band and where it came from, and puts the posting correction in as a request, because the band itself is set a level above this function.

perspectives.sees: A levelling grid and a band per grade, revised on the cycle at which compensation is reviewed.
perspectives.reads: A band set at the grade applies to everyone entering at that grade, which is what makes the hires consistent with one another.
perspectives.does: Revises the grid and applies it from the date of the revision. Processes already running against the previous figure are not rows in that decision.

perspectives.sees: Postings covered by a disclosure rule carry a range. A revision made mid-process reaches this layer only if the posting is checked against the offer.
perspectives.reads: The published range is a measurable object. The grade a candidate is assessed at, and the date a band was revised, are not covered by the same rule.
perspectives.does: Writes to what is enforceable: the presence of a range in the posting, and not the levelling decision that determines which range applies.

non_inferences: Does not prove intentional bait-and-switch malice unless verified by company policy evidence.

items.title: Take-home assignment exceeding reasonable stated scope
items.content:
# Take-home assignment exceeding reasonable stated scope

Take-home assignment requires building complex production-grade features demanding 20+ hours instead of stated 2–4 hours.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the company is harvesting free intellectual property for production use.
items.summary: Take-home assignment requires building complex production-grade features demanding 20+ hours instead of stated 2–4 hours.

probes.action: Define explicit boundaries and trade-offs in submission README stating assumptions made to fit the agreed timebox.
probes.expected_signal: Tests whether evaluators value scope management and communication over unbounded free work.

specimens.label: The assignment brief, as received
specimens.subject: Take-home exercise — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Build a service that ingests order events, deduplicates them, and exposes a query API over the resulting state.

Requirements: persistence with migrations, idempotent consumers, retry with backoff, structured logging, metrics endpoint, containerised local run, integration tests, and a short design document covering scaling and failure modes.
Please submit within one week. We estimate 2–4 hours.

specimens.reading: Count the deliverables against the stated budget. The mismatch is measurable, which makes it a fact rather than a feeling.

specimens.label: Asking about scope

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to do this. To fit the 2–4 hours, which parts should I treat as the core and which can I stub with a note in the README?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Ideally all of it — we use it to see how you work end to end.

specimens.reading: The stated budget and the expected deliverable are not reconciled when asked directly. That is the observation; the reason for it is not visible from here.

perspectives.sees: A brief with eight requirements listed against a stated budget of two to four hours, and an answer to the scoping question that leaves the list unchanged.
perspectives.reads: The stated time and the stated deliverables are two different sizes, and which of the two the submission will be scored against is not written anywhere the candidate can reach.
perspectives.does: Decides how many unpaid hours to commit, and submits with the timebox, the deliberate cuts and the assumptions written into the README, keeping the brief and the reply on record.

perspectives.sees: A candidate asking which parts are core, and a brief that is the only document the recruiter holds about this exercise.
perspectives.reads: A question about scope is a question about the rubric, and the rubric sits with the panel; the stage is measured by how quickly it clears.
perspectives.does: Answers from the brief, since that is what the recruiter has, and returns the thread to a submission date.

perspectives.sees: Finished submissions. How long any of them took is not a field in what reaches the panel.
perspectives.reads: Differences in completeness read as differences in level, because completeness is the variable the submissions expose.
perspectives.does: Compares the batch against itself rather than against the stated budget, and sets the bar from the fullest submission received.

non_inferences: Does not prove the company is harvesting free intellectual property for production use.

items.title: Multiple interview reschedulings or interviewer no-show
items.content:
# Multiple interview reschedulings or interviewer no-show

Interviews are repeatedly postponed, delayed at short notice, or interviewer fails to join scheduled call.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply candidate rejection; frequently reflects interviewer calendar congestion or emergency incidents.
items.summary: Interviews are repeatedly postponed, delayed at short notice, or interviewer fails to join scheduled call.

probes.action: Offer clear flexible availability slots and confirm contact details 2 hours prior to the call.
probes.expected_signal: Minimizes scheduling friction and verifies recruiter responsiveness.

specimens.label: Scheduling thread

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Tuesday 14:00 works for the panel — sending the invite now.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Apologies, the interviewer has a conflict. Can we move to Thursday same time?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Sorry to do this again — Thursday is out. Would Monday work?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Something urgent came up on the team. I will come back to you with new slots.

specimens.reading: Four movements, no interview. Record the dates: a pattern of postponement is evidence about the process, not about the candidate.

specimens.label: Calendar record

lines.text: Invite sent — Technical panel
Cancelled by organiser
Invite sent — Technical panel
Cancelled by organiser · no replacement issued

specimens.reading: Every cancellation came from the same side. That asymmetry is the observable part.

perspectives.sees: Four dates for one interview, invitations withdrawn by the organiser each time, and a fourth message with no replacement slot in it.
perspectives.reads: Something on the other side is moving, and which thing it is — a calendar, a panel, a requisition — is not in any message received.
perspectives.does: Records the dates and the wording, keeps other processes open, and asks for a date rather than for a reason.

perspectives.sees: Declines coming back from the panel's calendar, and no instruction about whether the search itself has changed.
perspectives.reads: A slot to reissue. Whether the requisition is still funded is not visible from the scheduling view.
perspectives.does: Sends new times and keeps the candidate in the pipeline; no cause arrives with the decline, so none travels onward.

perspectives.sees: One conflict on one morning, resolved by moving one invitation. The series exists in the candidate's inbox, not in the panel's calendar.
perspectives.reads: A week in which delivery and the loop need the same hours, and the loop is the part that can be moved.
perspectives.does: Releases the slot to the work the role exists to absorb and asks for a new time, each move decided on its own.

non_inferences: Does not imply candidate rejection; frequently reflects interviewer calendar congestion or emergency incidents.

items.title: Explicit feedback citing skill-depth shortfall
items.content:
# Explicit feedback citing skill-depth shortfall

Interviewer or recruiter provides structured notes citing a specific deficit in algorithmic complexity, architecture, or tool mastery.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply general incompetence; reflects threshold for this specific role level.
items.summary: Interviewer or recruiter provides structured notes citing a specific deficit in algorithmic complexity, architecture, or tool mastery.

probes.action: Review interview problem solution against industry standard patterns and identify edge cases missed.
probes.expected_signal: Verifies whether candidate code truly lacked required optimization or rigor.

specimens.label: Structured feedback notes
specimens.subject: Feedback — technical panel

lines.text: The panel was positive on system decomposition and on how you reasoned about failure modes.

The gap was in the second exercise: the solution was correct but quadratic, and the panel was looking for the linear approach using a hash index. We would want to see that reached without prompting at this level.
We are not moving forward now, but this was close and we would welcome a re-application in six months.

specimens.reading: A named exercise, a named property, a named expectation. This is the rare rejection that is actually actionable.

specimens.label: The moment in the panel

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: This works. What is the complexity?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Quadratic — nested scan over the same list.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Right. Can you get it down?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Probably with an index of some kind. I would want to think about it.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: That is fine, let us move on for time.

specimens.reading: The transcript and the written feedback agree. When they agree, the feedback is describing something that actually happened.

perspectives.sees: A rejection that names the exercise, the property of the solution and the expectation for the level, together with a stated window for re-application.
perspectives.reads: A threshold for this level in one named place, which is a claim that can be checked against what happened in the room.
perspectives.does: Checks the claim against their own record of the panel, and works from the two facts given: the named gap and the named window.

perspectives.sees: The panel's write-ups against the rubric, including the exercise where the step to the linear solution came after a prompt.
perspectives.reads: Evidence about the bar for the level rather than about the person; a decline can be revisited in six months and a hire cannot.
perspectives.does: Declines for now, keeps the exercise and the property in the notes, and leaves the re-application open.

perspectives.sees: A recommendation with a written reason attached to it, and none of the scoring that stands behind the reason.
perspectives.reads: A reason specific enough to send as written; the field it arrived in is free text, so what is in it is what the panel typed there.
perspectives.does: Sends the reason in the panel's own terms and adds the re-application window, and cannot expand on it if asked, because the scoring did not travel with it.

non_inferences: Does not imply general incompetence; reflects threshold for this specific role level.

items.title: Rejection within minutes of application submission
items.content:
# Rejection within minutes of application submission

Automated rejection email arrives within 2 to 30 minutes of form submission, outside human business hours.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply candidate resume was judged as poor by human engineers.
items.summary: Automated rejection email arrives within 2 to 30 minutes of form submission, outside human business hours.

probes.action: Audit application answers to mandatory knock-out questions (work permit, country of residence, minimum years experience).
probes.expected_signal: Identifies exact boolean filter rule triggered by ATS.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Your application

lines.text: Thank you for applying. After reviewing your application we have decided not to proceed at this time.
Sent 23:58 — eleven minutes after submission, outside working hours in every timezone the company operates in.

specimens.reading: The interval is the evidence. Eleven minutes at midnight describes the throughput of a rule, not the attention of a reader.

specimens.label: Application timeline

lines.text: Application submitted
Screening rules evaluated
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria
Notification email queued

specimens.reading: Two seconds between submission and decision. The eleven-minute delay was the mail queue, not deliberation.

perspectives.sees: A submission at 23:47 and a rejection at 23:58, outside working hours in every timezone the employer operates in.
perspectives.reads: Eleven minutes bounds how much reading could have happened; whether a person or a rule closed the record is not in the message.
perspectives.does: Reviews the answers given to the mandatory questions — permit, country, years of experience — because that is the only part of the decision the candidate holds a copy of.

perspectives.sees: A weekly figure: applications received, applications screened. This application sits inside the difference between the two and never enters the review queue.
perspectives.reads: The pipeline is a count against a capacity limit; a record closed at ingestion is not part of the work the queue holds.
perspectives.does: Works the queue that capacity allows, and answers a follow-up, if one arrives, from the status field, which reads that the minimum criteria were not met.

perspectives.sees: A submission, a rules evaluation two seconds later, a status transition and a queued notification. All four are events, and none of them is a reading of the profile.
perspectives.reads: The configuration ran as configured. Whether the criterion it enforced is the one the customer meant is not a value the platform holds.
perspectives.does: Emits the templated notification, records the disposition, and reports the interval as throughput on the dashboard the buyer evaluates.

non_inferences: Does not imply candidate resume was judged as poor by human engineers.

items.title: Communication mismatch or tone friction in panel
items.content:
# Communication mismatch or tone friction in panel

Noticeable divergence in communication style, pacing, or terminology during live panel discussions.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove candidate lacks teamwork skills globally.
items.summary: Noticeable divergence in communication style, pacing, or terminology during live panel discussions.

probes.action: Request explicit feedback on collaborative dynamic from recruiter.
probes.expected_signal: Clarifies whether friction was perceived as attitude issue or stylistic preference.

specimens.label: Panel discussion, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: So when you say the write path is eventually consistent, what does the client see?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Depends on the read. If it goes through the cache it can be stale by up to the TTL; if it goes to the primary it is current.

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: Sorry, I think we are talking past each other. I meant from the user perspective.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Ah — then: they may see their own write missing for a second or two.

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: That is what I was after.

specimens.reading: The disagreement was about which layer the question lived in, not about the answer. The content was right at both levels.

specimens.label: Panel feedback
specimens.subject: Feedback — architecture round

lines.text: Technically solid throughout.
The panel felt communication was not always calibrated to the audience — answers went to implementation detail where a product-level framing was wanted.

specimens.reading: Read against the transcript this is one exchange generalised into a trait. Both readings fit the same recording, which is exactly why the observation is not a verdict.

perspectives.sees: An exchange where the question and the answer sat at different levels, reconciled in the room within half a minute. Then written feedback that states the mismatch as a property of the answers.
perspectives.reads: One exchange and a generalisation of it both fit the same recording; which of the two the panel worked from is not in the note.
perspectives.does: Asks which moment the note refers to, and keeps the wording, since the note is the only version of the round that leaves the room.

perspectives.sees: Written impressions from each interviewer after the round. The recording is not what the panel reviews.
perspectives.reads: Wording that lines up across notes reads as a shared signal; a bad hire is visible for a year and has a name on it, a missed one has neither.
perspectives.does: Decides on the note as written, since it is the record of the round, and has no cheap way to test whether it describes one exchange or a pattern.

perspectives.sees: A summary line for the round: technically solid, communication not calibrated. What was said at minute twenty-two is not in the recruiter's view.
perspectives.reads: A reason to relay, at the level of detail it was given at.
perspectives.does: Passes the summary on, and when the candidate asks which moment it refers to, has the same sentence to answer with and nothing behind it.

non_inferences: Does not prove candidate lacks teamwork skills globally.

items.title: Offer rescinded or delayed due to internal freeze
items.content:
# Offer rescinded or delayed due to internal freeze

Candidate is verbally offered a role or receives written offer which is subsequently delayed or retracted before start date.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply candidate failed reference checks unless explicitly stated.
items.summary: Candidate is verbally offered a role or receives written offer which is subsequently delayed or retracted before start date.

probes.action: Request formal written notice regarding whether requisition is permanently cancelled or deferred to next fiscal quarter.
probes.expected_signal: Provides timeline clarity for candidate decision-making.

specimens.label: The offer, then the retraction
specimens.subject: Offer — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Day 0 — Delighted to confirm the offer we discussed. Start date 1 June, contract attached for signature.
Day 9 — I am very sorry to write this. A company-wide hiring freeze was announced this morning and all outstanding offers are suspended, including yours.
Day 9 — I understand you may have given notice. Please tell me if there is anything I can do, and I will be honest with you about what I can and cannot influence.

specimens.reading: Two dated documents about the same role. Whatever happens next, the fact that a written offer existed on day 0 is established, not remembered.

specimens.label: Establishing the scope of the freeze

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Is the freeze specific to the team, or company-wide?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Company-wide. Every open req is paused, and three other offers are in the same position as yours.

specimens.reading: The answer places the cause outside the hiring loop and outside the candidate. It also makes the claim checkable against public news.

perspectives.sees: A written offer with a start date, then a message before that date saying outstanding offers are suspended. Notice may already have been given at the current employer.
perspectives.reads: The stated cause sits above the hiring loop, and the message does not say whether the role is cancelled or deferred. Two dated documents about the same role now exist.
perspectives.does: Asks in writing whether the requisition is cancelled or deferred and to which quarter, keeps both messages, and reopens the processes that were paused.

perspectives.sees: An instruction that every open requisition is paused, arriving the same morning it arrives for everyone else, and a list of candidates to notify that includes one already holding a written offer.
perspectives.reads: The commitment that was conveyed rests on an authority the recruiter does not hold, and whether headcount returns this quarter is not visible from inside the funnel.
perspectives.does: Writes the message and chooses its wording. Can state the scope of the freeze and that other offers are in the same position; cannot give a start date.

perspectives.sees: A headcount decision applied to every open requisition at once. What reaches this layer is a count of paused requisitions and the spend it holds back.
perspectives.reads: A pause preserves optionality: an approved requisition that can be stopped costs less than one that cannot. Offers already extended are part of that count.
perspectives.does: Sets the scope of the freeze and the date it is reviewed. Resignations already handed in on the other side of those offers are not a figure this layer holds.

non_inferences: Does not imply candidate failed reference checks unless explicitly stated.

items.title: Unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by ghosting
items.content:
# Unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by ghosting

Recruiter initiates direct outreach expressing strong interest, but ceases communication after candidate responds with availability.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove candidate profile was rejected; often indicates batch automated sourcing campaigns.
items.summary: Recruiter initiates direct outreach expressing strong interest, but ceases communication after candidate responds with availability.

probes.action: Send one single polite follow-up after 5 business days referencing original outreach thread.
probes.expected_signal: Recovers stalled conversation if recruiter was out-of-office or overwhelmed.

specimens.label: Inbound outreach, then silence

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Hi! I came across your profile — your work on payment infrastructure is exactly what our team needs. Would you be open to a chat this week?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Thanks for reaching out. Yes, happy to talk. I am free Tuesday or Thursday after 15:00, and here is a short summary of what I have been working on.
— no reply —

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Following up in case this got buried. Still interested.
— no reply —

specimens.reading: The enthusiasm and the disappearance came from the same side, and the candidate did nothing between them except answer.

specimens.label: What was and was not established

lines.text: Established: an outreach message was sent on day 0; the candidate replied the same day with availability; two follow-ups went unanswered over eleven days.
Not established: whether the role existed, whether it was filled, whether anyone read the reply, or what the recruiter thought of the profile.

specimens.reading: Writing the two lists separately is the whole method. Most of the pain of this signal comes from filling the second list with guesses.

perspectives.sees: An inbound message naming their specific work, a same-day reply with availability, and then no answer — not to the availability, and not to a follow-up.
perspectives.reads: The approach and the silence came from the same side. Nothing in the thread separates a search that closed from a message no one opened.
perspectives.does: Sends one follow-up on the original thread, then treats the role as not live, and keeps the thread as a dated record of who started it.

perspectives.sees: A reply in an inbox that carries sourcing for several searches at once, beside a screening queue larger than the week's capacity.
perspectives.reads: A sourced reply is not an application, so it holds no position in the pipeline of record. Time-to-fill is measured; a thread with no requisition attached to it is not.
perspectives.does: Works the searches that are open now. Nothing in the queue raises the thread again, and no status message exists for a conversation that never became an application.

perspectives.sees: A sourcing sequence with a message sent and a reply received. The contact holds no application against any requisition.
perspectives.reads: A reply is a sequence outcome, not a pipeline stage. Nothing in the record marks the contact as awaiting an answer.
perspectives.does: Marks the sequence replied and stops sending. The expiry rule and the rejection template both key on an application, so neither fires here.

non_inferences: Does not prove candidate profile was rejected; often indicates batch automated sourcing campaigns.

items.title: Feedback stating candidate is overqualified for the grade
items.content:
# Feedback stating candidate is overqualified for the grade

Candidate is rejected on the grounds that their experience, seniority, or previous scope exceeds the open position tier.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply the candidate is undesirable, but signals retention/flight-risk and compensation mismatch concerns.
items.summary: Candidate is rejected on the grounds that their experience, seniority, or previous scope exceeds the open position tier.

probes.action: Inquire whether the organization has higher-tier or staff-level requisitions open where broader scope is desired.
probes.expected_signal: Channels candidate into appropriate leveling track.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Your application — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Thank you for the time you gave us over the past two weeks. The team enjoyed the conversation and rated your systems background highly.

After discussion we have decided not to move forward. Your experience sits above the band we scoped for this role, and we were concerned the day-to-day would not stay interesting for you for very long.
We would be glad to keep your profile on file and reach out when something at the right level opens up.

specimens.reading: The stated ground is fit with a band, not the quality of the work — and the risk named is retention, not capability.

specimens.label: Recruiter screen, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Your last role was a team lead position, is that right?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Formally, yes. In practice about two thirds of my week was hands-on.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Got it. I will be honest with you — my worry is that this role is a step down, and six months in you would be looking again.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Right now I am optimising for depth rather than scope.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Understood. I will pass that on either way.

specimens.reading: The concern is raised before any technical assessment: the level question is being settled ahead of the skill question.

perspectives.sees: A rejection naming experience above the band scoped for the role, and a retention concern raised at the screen, before any technical round.
perspectives.reads: The stated ground is fit with a band rather than the work shown. The message does not say whether a requisition at another level exists.
perspectives.does: Asks whether anything is open at a higher level, and records the stated reason and the date it was given.

perspectives.sees: A profile whose last title sits above the role, against a requisition opened at one band that the screen cannot move.
perspectives.reads: The level question is answerable now, and the same mismatch found at offer stage costs the search weeks. What the hiring manager will accept at this level is not written down anywhere the recruiter can read it.
perspectives.does: Raises the concern on the call and passes the answer on. Changing the band is not theirs to do; the wording of the rejection is.

perspectives.sees: A candidate who has previously held a wider scope than the role carries, assessed at the level the requisition was opened at.
perspectives.reads: A hire who leaves early is visible and attributed to the person who made it; a candidate declined on level leaves no record anyone reads later.
perspectives.does: Declines at this band, or asks for the level to be reconsidered, which means a different requisition funded elsewhere.

perspectives.sees: One requisition approved at one band, and a levelling grid that defines what sits above it. Individual candidates do not reach this layer.
perspectives.reads: One band per requisition is what keeps offers consistent and defensible across every hire. A person declined at the edge of the grid is not an event this layer records.
perspectives.does: Holds the requisition at the approved band. Opening one at a higher level is a separate funding decision on a quarterly cycle.

non_inferences: Does not imply the candidate is undesirable, but signals retention/flight-risk and compensation mismatch concerns.

items.title: Conflicting feedback across different interviewers
items.content:
# Conflicting feedback across different interviewers

Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove bad faith; highlights lack of rubric calibration across the hiring committee.
items.summary: Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

probes.action: Request aggregated hiring rubric summary from talent partner.
probes.expected_signal: Reveals whether team had misaligned internal evaluation criteria.

specimens.label: Two rounds, two verdicts
specimens.subject: Consolidated feedback

lines.text: Round 2 (systems): Strong architectural depth. Reasoned clearly about consistency trade-offs and failure modes. Recommend proceed.
Round 4 (technical): Insufficient depth for the level. Struggled to move past a first-pass solution. Recommend do not proceed.
Final decision: do not proceed.

specimens.reading: Both notes are about the same person in the same week. At least one of them is measuring something other than the candidate.

specimens.label: What the two rounds actually asked

lines.speaker: Interviewer B
lines.text: Round 2 — Walk me through how you would keep two regions in sync when the link between them drops.

lines.speaker: Interviewer D
lines.text: Round 4 — Here is a string parsing problem. You have twenty-five minutes.

specimens.reading: The rounds did not disagree about the candidate; they measured different things and reported both as depth.

perspectives.sees: Two verdicts from the same week: one round rating architectural depth highly, another finding depth insufficient for the level, and one negative decision under them.
perspectives.reads: The rounds asked different questions and both reported the answer as depth. Which of the two the decision rests on is not stated.
perspectives.does: Asks for the consolidated rubric summary, and records what each round actually asked alongside what each concluded.

perspectives.sees: Two written notes on the same candidate from rounds they did not sit in, each using the word depth for a different exercise.
perspectives.reads: Those notes are the whole of what is available about those rounds; nothing in them separates a disagreement about the candidate from a difference between the two exercises.
perspectives.does: Sets who interviews and what each round asks, and closes the split with a decision rather than a re-run. A hire made over a recorded negative note carries their name if it goes wrong.

perspectives.sees: Two recommendations pointing opposite ways and a decision line under them. The scores behind each recommendation are not in the recruiter's view.
perspectives.reads: One reason has to be written to the candidate out of two notes that do not agree. Anything said beyond the recorded decision can be quoted back later.
perspectives.does: Sends the outcome in wording that stays inside what was written down, and moves the requisition on. Reopening a recorded decision sits with the hiring manager, not the recruiter.

non_inferences: Does not prove bad faith; highlights lack of rubric calibration across the hiring committee.
